name: Why do pool resurfacing quotes leave out startup and chemical balancing?

mainEntity.name: Should startup chemicals and water balancing be part of the resurfacing bid or treated as a separate cost?
mainEntity.text: Should startup chemicals and water balancing be part of the resurfacing bid or treated as a separate cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Startup is not just a maintenance detail; it protects the new finish during its most vulnerable period. Some resurfacing bids include initial chemical balancing, brushing instructions, and a startup visit, while others leave those items to the homeowner. That difference matters because the wrong water chemistry in the first days after fill can stain, etch, or weaken the surface. Homeowners comparing bids should verify whether the estimate covers startup chemicals, water testing, brush visits, and guidance for the first 7 to 28 days. If those items are missing, the real project price is higher than it appears. A complete bid should explain who is responsible for balancing the water and how the contractor verifies that the surface is being cared for correctly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Startup and chemical balancing are often excluded from basic resurfacing bids even though they are critical to finish performance. Some contractors include them, while others treat them as an add-on or homeowner responsibility. If startup is missing from the quote, the project may look cheaper than it really is.
